subject: Radiological Signs
title: Abdominal & Neuro Radiology Pearls
preview: Classic abdominal and brain imaging signs connect shape to disease but still need full-context interpretation.

sections.title: Obstruction signs in abdominal imaging
points: Coffee-bean sign: a markedly dilated twisted sigmoid colon in some presentations of sigmoid volvulus.
Bird-beak sign: tapered gastroesophageal junction on contrast studies of achalasia; other disorders can mimic it.

sections.title: Luminal narrowing patterns
points: Apple-core narrowing is a classic colonic contrast-imaging clue for annular colorectal carcinoma but is not by itself a histologic diagnosis.
A string-like narrowed segment in ileal imaging can be seen in Crohn disease, interpreted alongside other findings.

sections.title: Head CT extra-axial blood
points: Epidural hematoma is often biconvex; subdural blood is often crescentic.
Suture boundaries, anatomical location and chronicity affect the imaging appearance and differential.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: A classic image silhouette is a clue, not a universal rule or replacement for clinical evaluation.

quickRevision: Coffee-bean appearance can be associated with sigmoid volvulus; a bird-beak narrowing may occur in achalasia.
An apple-core colonic lesion suggests a constricting process requiring further investigation.
Extra-axial hemorrhage patterns on CT are classically lens-shaped for epidural and crescentic for subdural bleeding, with exceptions.

quiz.question: A crescent-shaped extra-axial collection is classically associated with what?
options: Epidural hematoma with a biconvex shape
